subject: DSCR loans: when they save the deal, when they're a trap
preheader: When DTI doesn't pencil · 8-9% typical rate band · The 1.20 floor that decides everything

marketSnapshot.headline: DSCR loans qualify the property, not you
marketSnapshot.body: DSCR (Debt Service Coverage Ratio) loans are investor-targeted mortgages that qualify based on the property's rental income, not your personal DTI or tax returns. Useful when you're scaling and conventional financing slots run out, or when your W-2 income doesn't support more conventional deals. The tradeoff: rates run 100-200bp higher than conventional, and most DSCR lenders require a 1.20-1.25 DSCR floor. Worth understanding before you assume DSCR is the answer to every financing problem.

dealSpotter.body: $685k 3-unit. Your W-2 doesn't support another conventional loan after the first few. DSCR lender qualifies the property at 1.23 ratio. You pay ~130bp more on rate, which costs ~$300/mo on the loan vs conventional. Still cash-flow positive. The premium is the cost of being able to keep buying without DTI as a constraint.

dealSpotter.address: Example: conventional also works — take it
dealSpotter.headlineNumber: DSCR 1.35 · BUT conventional clears DTI too
dealSpotter.body: $285k SFR. DSCR pencils easily. But your W-2 + existing rental income clears conventional DTI as well. Pricing comparison: DSCR 8.3% vs conventional 6.95% = 135bp spread = ~$320/mo difference. Take conventional. DSCR is a fallback when conventional doesn't work, not a default.

$575k 3/2. The property's gross rent barely covers debt service at DSCR loan rates. DSCR comes in at 1.04 — below the typical 1.20 floor. The lenders who will fund at 1.05+ charge 9.5%+ which actually makes the deal cash-flow negative. The DSCR floor isn't arbitrary — it represents the lender's risk math. When you're scraping under it, the deal is too tight.

blogFeature.title: DSCR loans explained: rates, requirements, and when they make sense
blogFeature.excerpt: DSCR loans qualify the property, not you — but the trade-off is +100-200bp over conventional rates and a 1.20-1.25 ratio floor. The cases where DSCR is the only path forward + the cases where it's a trap.

qa.question: I have 3 conventional rental loans already and my DTI is tight. Should I switch to DSCR for my next deal?
qa.answer: Probably yes, but understand the trade-off. The +100-200bp rate premium compounds over the holding period — on a $300k loan over 10 years, ~$300/mo of extra interest is $36k of lifetime cost vs. conventional. Math that against the alternative (don't buy at all, wait until you can clear conventional DTI). If you'd otherwise sit on the sidelines for 12-24 months, the DSCR premium is the cost of continuing to deploy capital. Practical tactics that reduce friction: shop multiple DSCR lenders (rate spread across DSCR lenders is wider than conventional — 30-50bp variance is normal), put down 25-30% instead of the minimum (improves DSCR ratio AND lowers rate), and structure for a 5-year interest-only period if available (lower payment = better DSCR + more cash flow during hold).
